New spec IDs or components arrived. Read `steps.md` before changing a step table or the planned layout, and `template.md` for a new pipeline's format. Ends at the Review Gate in `../SKILL.md`.

# Steps, layout and readability rules

Read before writing or changing a step table or the planned layout. The file format is `template.md`.

## Steps

Per pipeline:
- **Entry** `src/<path>/<entry module>::run_<workflow>`, in the pipeline's own entry module (Layout), **Trigger** (a CLI command or a call from another pipeline), **Purpose** (one sentence a newcomer understands: what running it gives the user, not how; `dt explain` leads with it), **Covers** (spec IDs, including whole-run `QR-` IDs; a constraint a decision meets, such as a data source's licence under AD-02, goes on the Covers of the step that applies it).
- **Step table**, one row per call in order, plus a row per library class (below): Step (function name; `PL-NN.<function>` is its ID), Owner (one component, or component.module; a step with two owners is two steps), In → Out, Spine version, Covers. A step another pipeline provides says `PL-01 as built`; one following a reference cites it (`as RF-01, per-window fit`).
- **In → Out names contract types.** Every Out, and every In another step's Out feeds, is a contract `type` section (`Demand → Profile` resolves to `### profile.Profile: type`; qualify as `profile.Profile` only when two components define the name), and every CamelCase name in the cell must resolve to one. Entry arguments (dates, regions, a config field) and the last step's plain result (a path, frames) stay lower-case. The build freezes each of these types first, with a sample, so every step's spine and tests start at once against it. A type the contract lacks is a contract change: list it and route to `architecture-design` Revise; never invent it here. `dt lint` checks it (`step-io-types`).
- **Library classes are steps.** A class a factory or lookup step returns, which the pipeline then drives through a Protocol (`make_dataset` returning `SingleCropSet` as a `Dataset`), gets its own row right after its factory's: Step the class name, Owner its module, In → Out its constructor's input → the Protocol, Spine version a minimal real class (200 synthetic leaves, a model guessing at random). The entry sketch never calls it, but the build gives it a spine of its own, so wiring waits on that spine, never on the class's upgrade. Two classes behind one factory are two rows. The same holds for any contract function or class a step calls (`methods.make_learner`, `runlog.RunWriter`, `store.append_parts`): its own row, unless it lives in the calling step's owner folder (`train.loop` → `train/loop/`). No spine builds a contract symbol beyond its own step.
- **A provider waiting on a probe** (an external API whose probe isn't Answered or Waived) sits behind a Protocol, and the milestone gets a stand-in: a synthetic class row behind the same factory, in a sibling owner folder (`data.weather_synthetic` → `data/weather_synthetic/`), selected by settings. The real provider keeps its row; `build-planning` plans its spine once the probe is Answered.
- **References** (optional): `**References:** RF-01 (remove_seasonality)` after Covers. Never a `references/` path.
- **Entry sketch** (pre-build): calls to the steps in table order and a return, nothing else. A loop, branch or computation is a missing step.

**Contract `Used by:` lines** get the calling PL IDs after the consumer components; symbol IDs are component-qualified even in a single package (`### profile.fit_seasonality: …`).

**Multi-package:** cross-package *system pipelines* are `architecture-design`'s, in the root. A package-local pipeline that is one segment of one names it: `**Entry:** … · **Trigger:** … · **Part of:** PL-05`. Never edit the root.

## Changing a step table

Revise, and Sync when the doc changes, edit an existing table this way:

- Keep step names where the function survives; a split step gets new rows with new function names. Keep the pipeline's ID: a rebuilt package keeps its PL IDs where it can, so its golden cases still apply.
- If the entry sketch is gone (the spine was built), don't recreate it. The step table is the contract the code must match; the code change becomes a task.
- Keep `Used by:` lines true: add the PL ID to a symbol a new step calls, and remove it from one no step of that pipeline calls any more.

## Layout

One entry module per pipeline, never shared, so two pipelines' wiring never touches one file: `pipeline.py` in the component (single package) or package whose only pipeline it is; where a component runs several, `pipelines/pl<NN>_<workflow>.py` each, and an existing `pipeline.py` stays as it is. One module per step owner (`profile.fit` → `profile/fit.py`; an owner given only as `profile` gets one module per related group of steps), never named like a generated file (`api.schema` beside a generated `api/schema.ts`: call it `api.schema_check`). A step whose module needs private helpers owns a folder instead (`core.train` → `core/train/`), holding them; no other step's code goes inside it. A step with its own upgrade beyond the spine gets its own module (`validate/flags.py`, `validate/coverage.py`), so its thicken task never shares a file; only steps built and thickened together share one. In a single package each component gets a subfolder whose `__init__.py` exports its contract only, so a later Grow is a folder move. Modules on no step: only `__init__.py`, the entry modules, `__main__.py` for a `python -m` trigger (dispatching each trigger to its entry), and `types.py`. Test folders sit at the repo root in every layout, multi-package included: `tests/intent/<pkg>/`, `tests/unit/<pkg>/`, never under the package's folder. Plan against `build-setup`'s size bar (500 lines per module, 60 per function, or `CONSTRAINTS.md`'s values): split a module expected to pass it now.

## Readability rules

`build-setup` copies these into `CONSTRAINTS.md`; builders and reviewers enforce them.

- One entry function per pipeline, reading as calls to its named steps; each step owned by one component, its function living there.
- No registries, plugin dispatch or config-driven wiring unless an `AD-NN` says so. A new abstraction needs a second real implementation or a seam the architecture named.
- Every spine version is real and minimal, often the baseline, never a mock, stub or hard-coded return; it stays as what upgrades must beat. Only a step calling another pipeline or package may run against that boundary's fixture-backed fake, until the milestone's system task swaps in the real provider; a step consuming another step's output is built and tested on that type's frozen sample, never on a fake of the step. An object with behavior (a Protocol or class) or a call into another component's function is frozen as its Protocol or signature plus a fixture-backed replay double, which is that type's sample, not a fake.
- A decision-backed exception goes on the row or pipeline, citing it (`dataset lookup by name (AD-06)`).
----
# pipelines.md template

The file format every mode writes. `dt` parses it: keep the header line, the `## PL-NN: Title` headings, the six step-table columns and the `(pre-build — removed by spine task)` headings exactly. The rules for filling it are in `steps.md`.

- Multi-package layout: the code block starts at the package's path from the root architecture (`packages/<pkg>/src/<pkg>/`); the test line stays `tests/intent/<pkg>/  tests/unit/<pkg>/`, at the repo root (`steps.md`, Layout).

# RL Lab — Architecture

**Status:** Approved · **Shape:** Single package · **Last updated:** 2026-10-18 · **Spec:** [spec.md](spec.md)

## Overview
One Python package, `rllab`, run from the command line, holding two environments (Snake and the fish tank) on one shared core. A training run builds one environment setup (Snake with a reward, or the tank with a fish count and a view) and one learner from the registry. It plays games from seeds derived from the run seed, and hands every acting agent's move to the learner: Snake's one snake, or every fish in the tank sharing one policy. At each of 20 curve points it pauses training to play the setup's 100 reserved test games greedily, then writes the point to the run's folder. When the run finishes it saves the agent and its test games and marks the run's status last. Comparisons read only complete runs and write one report per environment, handing the per-game scores to the `null-hypothesis-testing` skill. The replay viewer rebuilds any saved game by stepping the environment through its saved moves, and draws Snake's move scores or each fish's swim arrow and spread. Training, testing, storage, comparison and replay see only the `core` protocols and the registry, never an environment or a learner (AD-04, AD-11).

flowchart LR
  cli --> train & compare & replay
  train --> registry & evaluate & store
  registry --> snake & tank & baselines & tabular & dqn & pg
  baselines --> snake & tank
  replay --> registry & evaluate & store
  compare --> store
  store --> evaluate
  snake & tank & baselines & tabular & dqn & pg & evaluate & store --> core

114	### AD-05: Seeds, test-seed reservation and CPU determinism
115	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-18 · **Scope:** system
116	- **Context:** RUN-03 needs identical curves on a rerun; SNAKE-08, TANK-13, TAB-03, DQN-06, PG-07 and REPLAY-07 need repeatable games; EVAL-01 needs test seeds never used in training; RUN-09 needs Snake's draws untouched by the tank.
117	- **Decision:** A run seed builds a `np.random.SeedSequence`, spawned into separate generators for training game seeds, move choice (exploration or sampling from the policy), batch sampling and network initialisation (a `torch.Generator`), the same four for every learner and environment. Test seeds are 0–99; training game seeds are drawn from `[1_000, 2^31)`. Torch runs with `torch.set_num_threads(1)` and `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`. Each game owns its own generator from its game seed, so food placement, the ball's start direction and the fish's start spots depend only on the seed and the moves.
118	- **Alternatives:** A global seed (`np.random.seed`): any new random call shifts every later draw. Several threads: faster on big networks, but the reduction order varies between runs.
119	- **Consequences:** Results reproduce on the same laptop and library versions, not across machines; `settings.json` records the versions. One thread stays fast enough for these networks (Risks).

158	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-18 · **Scope:** system

165	### AD-12: One policy-gradient learner, Gaussian swims, the rung a setting
166	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-18 · **Scope:** pg
167	- **Context:** UR-52: "I want it to be a good fit for policy-gradient / PPO and continuous control". PG-01–PG-04 build four rungs; PG-05 requires each to differ only by the added piece; PG-06 shares one policy across fish; PG-07 samples in training and takes the most likely move in tests; REPLAY-09 shows each fish's spread; PG-08 forbids library algorithms.
168	- **Decision:** `pg.PGAgent` takes a `PGSettings` whose `rung` is `reinforce`, `baseline`, `actor_critic` or `ppo`. The policy is a diagonal Gaussian over the swim velocity (x, y): an MLP 11 → 64 → 64 → 4 gives the mean and the log spread of each axis for the fish's own view, the log spread clamped to [−5, 1]. Training samples a move from the move-choice generator; tests take the mean; the replay shows the mean of the two spreads. The fish learns from the move it sampled; the tank caps the speed. Log-probabilities, discounted returns, advantages, losses and the clipped ratio are written in `pg`. Each rung adds one piece: `baseline` subtracts a separate critic (11 → 64 → 64 → 1) trained toward the returns; `actor_critic` replaces the return with the one-step estimate, learning every `steps_per_update` steps; `ppo` makes `passes` clipped passes over each batch in minibatches. `reinforce` and `baseline` update once every agent's experience has ended.
169	- **Alternatives:** A spread that doesn't depend on the view: steadier, and usual for PPO, but every fish would show the same number at every step, so REPLAY-09 would say nothing. PPO with generalised advantage estimation: the textbook form, but it adds a second piece to the PPO rung, against PG-05. Discrete swim directions: fits value learning, not the continuous control UR-52 asks for.
170	- **Consequences:** The four rungs share one code path, each step testable against a hand-computed value. The PPO rung is weaker than the textbook one, which is a result to explain (EVAL-06), not a defect. Later variants (generalised advantages, say) add a rung value.

174	**Status:** Accepted · **Date:** 2026-10-18 · **Scope:** tank
175	- **Context:** TANK-02 needs a mirror bounce at a constant speed; TANK-04 a move every 0.1 s capped at 2.5 units per second; TANK-05 a wall stop; TANK-07 removal at the end of each step; TANK-13 identical games from a seed. QR-01 needs a 5-fish PPO run and its test games inside 60 minutes.

189	## Risks and open questions
190	- One CPU thread might not fit a run plus 20 × 100 test games inside 60 minutes (QR-01): a DQN run on Snake, and above all 5-fish PPO, whose test games are up to 600 steps each. Mitigation: the first DQN task and the first tank PPO task each time 10,000 steps and one round of test games, and the step budget is set from that. Test games can be stepped as a batch if needed.
191	- The table learner sees at most 2^11 situations but only a few hundred occur; it may plateau well below the scripted bot. That is a result to explain (EVAL-06), not a defect.
192	- Determinism (RUN-03, RUN-09) holds only on the same laptop and library versions. `settings.json` records them, and the rerun check compares like with like.
193	- The tank's time cap ends experience like a removal (AD-11), but a fish's view has no clock, so the critic of the upper rungs sees the same view end in very different returns. It may learn slower; a result to explain. Counting the cap as a cut-off would be a change to AD-11 and AD-12.
194	- A view-dependent spread (AD-12) can collapse or blow up; the clamp bounds it, and the curve shows it (the PG edge case).
195	- M1's plan was approved against the earlier contract. On approval, `pipeline-design` updates PL-01–PL-03 for these contracts and the tank, `test-planning` adds tank cases and a RUN-09 case, and `build-planning` rechecks M1's interface task before the build starts.
196	- Grow: 14 components and a contract well over 200 lines trip the size trigger; the lab stays one package (UR-34, UR-38, UR-65).

- **TANK-01** The tank is a circle of radius 10 holding one ball and a fixed number of fish, 1 or 5, saved with the run.

- **TANK-02** The ball, of radius 0.5, moves at a constant 2 units per second and bounces off the tank wall like a mirror.
  - Given the ball reaching the wall, when it bounces, then it leaves at the same angle to the wall's normal as it arrived, on the other side of the normal.
  - Given any step of any game, when the ball's speed is measured, then it is 2 units per second.

<!-- docs/spec.md:272 -->
- **TANK-03** Each game starts with the ball at the centre heading in a direction set by the game seed, and each fish at a seed-chosen spot between 5 units from the centre and the wall.
  - Given any game, when it starts, then the ball is at the centre and every fish is between 5 and 9.75 units from the centre.
  - Given the same game seed twice, when both games start, then the ball's direction and every fish's spot are identical.

<!-- docs/spec.md:275 -->
- **TANK-04** Every 0.1 seconds of tank time, each fish still swimming chooses a move: a swim velocity (x, y) in tank directions, capped at a speed of 2.5 units per second.
  - Given a fish that chooses velocity (1, 0), when the step runs, then it moves 0.1 units in the x direction.
  - Given a fish that chooses velocity (3, 4), when the step runs, then it swims at 2.5 units per second in direction (0.6, 0.8) and moves 0.25 units.

<!-- docs/spec.md:278 -->
- **TANK-05** A fish, of radius 0.25, can't leave the tank: a move that would carry it past the wall stops it at the wall.
  - Given a fish touching the wall that swims straight outward, when the step runs, then it stays inside the tank, touching the wall.

<!-- docs/spec.md:280 -->
- **TANK-06** Fish swim through each other unharmed.
  - Given two fish whose paths cross, when the step runs, then both finish their moves and both are still swimming.

<!-- docs/spec.md:282 -->
- **TANK-07** At the end of each step, the ball removes every fish whose edge touches it (centres within 0.75 units); a removed fish takes no more moves and is no longer seen by other fish.
  - Given a fish whose centre ends a step 0.7 units from the ball's centre, when the step ends, then the fish is removed.
  - Given a fish whose centre ends a step 0.8 units from the ball's centre, when the step ends, then the fish is still swimming.
  - Given a removed fish, when the other fish's views are read, then none of them sees it.

<!-- docs/spec.md:286 -->
- **TANK-08** A tank game ends when every fish is removed, or at 60 seconds of tank time (600 steps); until then it goes on for the fish still swimming.
  - Given 5 fish of which 4 are removed, when the steps continue, then the game goes on until the last fish is removed or 600 steps have run.
  - Given a fish still swimming after 600 steps, when the 600th step ends, then the game ends.

<!-- docs/spec.md:289 -->
- **TANK-09** A fish's reward is +0.1 for each step it survives, and 0 for the step in which it is removed, which ends its experience; there is no other reward.
  - Given a fish that survives a step, when the step ends, then its reward is +0.1.
  - Given a fish removed during a step, when the step ends, then its reward is 0 and it has no further steps.
  - Given a fish that survives all 600 steps, when its rewards are summed, then the total is 60.

<!-- docs/spec.md:293 -->
- **TANK-10** A fish's score is the seconds of tank time it survived, from 0 to 60, and a game's score is the mean over all its fish, removed ones included.
  - Given 5 fish that survive 10, 20, 30, 60 and 60 seconds, when the game is scored, then its score is 36.
  - Given 1 fish removed at 12.5 seconds, when the game is scored, then its score is 12.5.

<!-- docs/spec.md:296 -->
- **TANK-11** At every step, each fish sees exactly 11 numbers about what lies within its view radius: for the ball, whether it is seen, its position relative to the fish (2 numbers) and its velocity relative to the fish (2); for the wall, whether it is seen and the offset from the fish to the wall's nearest point (2); for the nearest other fish, whether it is seen and its position relative to the fish (2). Anything beyond the radius is seen as no, and its numbers are 0.
  - Given the short view and the ball 3 units away, when the fish's view is read, then the ball is seen as yes and its relative position and velocity are the true ones.
  - Given the short view and the ball 5 units away, when the view is read, then the ball is seen as no and its 4 numbers are 0.
  - Given the short view and a fish at the centre of the tank, when the view is read, then the wall is seen as no and its 2 numbers are 0.
  - Given a 1-fish game, when the view is read, then the nearest other fish is seen as no and its 2 numbers are 0.

<!-- docs/spec.md:301 -->
- **TANK-12** A fish's view radius is either 4 units (the short view) or 20 units (the wide view, which spans the whole tank), saved with the run.
  - Given the wide view, when any fish's view is read at any step, then the ball and the wall are seen as yes, and so is the nearest other fish if one is still swimming.

<!-- docs/spec.md:303 -->
- **TANK-13** The same game seed and the same moves always give the same game.
  - Given a game seed and a list of moves for every fish, when the game is played twice, then every position, removal, reward and ending is identical.

<!-- docs/spec.md:81 -->
- **BASE-04** The tank's random swimmer picks each move with a uniformly random direction and a speed drawn uniformly from 0 to 2.5 units per second.
  - Given 10,000 random-swimmer moves, when their directions are sorted into four equal quarters of the circle, then each quarter holds between 23% and 27% of them.
  - Given 10,000 random-swimmer moves, when their speeds are averaged, then the mean is between 1.2 and 1.3.

<!-- docs/spec.md:84 -->
- **BASE-05** When the tank's scripted bot sees the ball, it swims at 2.5 units per second directly away from the ball.
  - Given the ball seen at relative position (1, 0), when the bot moves, then its swim velocity is (−2.5, 0).

<!-- docs/spec.md:86 -->
- **BASE-06** When the tank's scripted bot doesn't see the ball, it stays still.
  - Given the ball seen as no, when the bot moves, then its swim velocity is (0, 0).

<!-- docs/spec.md:88 -->
- **BASE-07** In each comparison, the tank baselines play with the same fish count and view radius as the learner they are compared with.
  - Given a 5-fish, wide-view learner, when its baselines are scored, then they play the same test tanks with 5 fish and the wide view.

<!-- docs/spec.md:325 -->
- **PG-01** The REINFORCE rung, after each game, raises the chance of each move a fish made in proportion to the discounted return that followed it.
  - Given a known policy, a finished game, the run's learning rate and discount, when one update is applied, then the change to the policy equals the hand-computed REINFORCE step.

<!-- docs/spec.md:327 -->
- **PG-02** The learned-baseline rung weights each move by its return minus a learned estimate of the return from the situation it was made in, and trains that estimate toward the returns seen.
  - Given a move with return 4.0 from a situation estimated at 3.0, when its weight is computed, then the weight is 1.0.
  - Given a situation whose estimate is below the returns seen from it, when the estimate is trained, then the estimate rises toward them.

<!-- docs/spec.md:330 -->
- **PG-03** The actor-critic rung weights each move by its reward plus the discounted estimate of the next situation, minus the estimate of the situation it was made in, and learns after every fixed number of steps saved with the run's settings.
  - Given a known reward, discount and two estimates, when a move's weight is computed, then it equals the hand-computed value.
  - Given the run's steps per update, when training runs, then an update happens after every that many steps, not only at the end of a game.

<!-- docs/spec.md:333 -->
- **PG-04** The PPO rung learns from each batch of experience in a fixed number of passes, and caps each move's change in chance at a clip range, both saved with the run's settings.
  - Given a move whose chance has already risen past 1 + the clip range times its chance when collected, and a positive weight, when the update is computed, then that move pushes the policy no further.
  - Given the run's passes per batch, when one batch is learned from, then the number of passes equals it.

<!-- docs/spec.md:336 -->
- **PG-05** Each tank setup differs from the one it is compared with only by the piece it adds: one rung from the rung below, 5-fish PPO from 1-fish PPO only by the fish count, and wide-view PPO from short-view PPO only by the view radius.
  - Given the saved settings of any two setups compared in EVAL-05, when they are compared, then the only differences are the added piece and its own settings.

<!-- docs/spec.md:338 -->
- **PG-06** With several fish, every fish uses the same policy on its own view, and every fish's experience trains it.
  - Given a 5-fish run, when moves are chosen, then every fish's move comes from the one policy applied to that fish's own 11 numbers.
  - Given a 5-fish run, when an update is applied, then it learns from the experience of all 5 fish up to each one's removal.

<!-- docs/spec.md:341 -->
- **PG-07** While training, each fish picks its move at random from the policy's spread; during test games it takes the policy's most likely move.
  - Given a trained policy, when a test game is played twice from the same seed, then both games are identical.

<!-- docs/spec.md:343 -->
- **PG-08** The learning updates of every rung are written in the project; no ready-made learning algorithm is used.
  - Given any trained rung, when its learning steps are traced, then each one is code written in the project.

<!-- docs/spec.md:250 -->
- **REPLAY-08** A tank replay shows the tank, the ball, every fish still swimming, the time in seconds, the number of fish still swimming, and the time each removed fish was removed.
  - Given a tank replay at any step, when it is shown, then all of these are visible; at the end, the ending (every fish removed, or the 60-second cap) is shown.

<!-- docs/spec.md:252 -->
- **REPLAY-09** At every step of a tank learner's game, each fish still swimming shows an arrow for its chosen swim velocity and a number for how sure it was: the spread of its move choice, smaller meaning surer.
  - Given a policy-gradient replay at any step, when it is shown, then every fish still swimming has an arrow and a spread number.
  - Given a tank baseline replay, when it is shown, then the arrows and spreads are shown as not applicable.

<!-- docs/spec.md:186 -->
- **RUN-09** After the fish tank is added, Snake runs saved before it still reproduce, compare and replay identically.
  - Given a Snake run saved before the tank was added, when it is rerun on the same laptop from its saved settings and seed, then the test score at every curve point is identical to the saved one.
  - Given the Snake comparisons and replays made before the tank was added, when they are made again, then every result and every replayed game is identical.

<!-- docs/spec.md:184 -->
- **RUN-08** Training, testing, saving evidence and replay work for a second environment without changes to them.
  - Given a minimal second environment used only for this check, when it is trained, tested and replayed, then none of the training, testing, saving or replay behavior had to change.

<!-- docs/spec.md:217 -->
- **EVAL-07** Each environment is done when its top learner beats the random player, beats or ties the scripted bot, every comparison in EVAL-04 and EVAL-05 for that environment has a result, and every tie and no-difference result is explained. Snake's top learner is the Double DQN agent; the tank's is 5-fish, short-view PPO.
  - Given a Double DQN agent that beats both baselines and all comparisons made and explained, when the done check runs, then it reports done.
  - Given a Double DQN agent that ties the scripted bot with the tie explained, when the done check runs, then it reports done.
  - Given a tie with the scripted bot left unexplained, when the done check runs, then it reports not done and names the missing explanation.
  - Given a Double DQN agent that ties or loses to the random player, when the done check runs, then it reports not done.
  - Given 5-fish, short-view PPO that beats the random swimmer, ties the scripted bot with the tie explained, and every tank comparison made and explained, when the done check runs, then it reports the tank done.
  - Given 5-fish, wide-view PPO that beats the scripted bot while 5-fish, short-view PPO loses to it, when the done check runs, then it reports the tank not done.

<!-- docs/spec.md:357 -->
- **QR-01** Each training run in either environment, including its test games, finishes in under 1 hour (60 minutes) on the laptop's processor.
  - Checked by the elapsed time saved with each run; RUN-07 stops any run that reaches 60 minutes.
